questions.q: What does the lesson say a whiteboard round tests, beyond technical knowledge?
options: Nothing -- only the final design matters
Typing speed
Memorization of exact Salesforce limits
Communication -- the whiteboard performance itself is graded alongside the architecture
questions.explain: The lesson states that whiteboarding adds a performance/communication layer that is evaluated alongside the technical content.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend explaining your design while you draw rather than only after it's finished?
options: Because silence while drawing reads as uncertainty even when the candidate is confident
Because talking while drawing is required by Salesforce certification rules
Because the panel cannot hear you otherwise
Because drawing and talking at the same time is impossible, so it must be sequenced
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states that explaining as you draw prevents silence from being read as uncertainty.

questions.q: In the lesson's six-step whiteboarding structure, what comes immediately after sketching objects and relationships?
options: Talking through scale
Ending the session
Adding the security model as boundaries around the objects
Asking the panel to leave
questions.explain: The lesson's structure moves from objects and relationships to the security model next, before integration and automation.

questions.q: In the fictional Fairmont Logistics example, why does the lesson say clarifying whether status updates are real-time or batch matters so early?
options: It doesn't matter and can be decided at the very end
Because that single answer changes the integration pattern the rest of the design is built around
Because Fairmont Logistics is a real client with a documented requirement
Because batch updates are always the correct choice regardless of requirements
questions.explain: The lesson notes that this clarifying question changes the integration approach fundamentally, so it should be resolved before designing further.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about leaving space on the whiteboard early in a session?
options: Leaving space matters because a board that's full early has nowhere to go when a follow-up question needs a new element added
It should be avoided -- fill the board immediately to look prepared
Whiteboard space has no effect on the session
Only the interviewer is allowed to decide how much space is used
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly advises leaving space so follow-up questions can be accommodated without running out of room.
